source.title: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
source.authors: Weijia Shi; Jaechan Lee; Yangsibo Huang; Sadhika Malladi; Jie-Yu Zhao; Ari Holtzman; Daogao Liu; Luke S. Zettlemoyer; Noah A. Smith; Chi-Yuan Zhang

record.file_problem: No apparent problem; the full paper, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether unlearning reduces targeted knowledge memorization while preserving utility, using its own benchmark and measures. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The study measures knowledge memorization on the forget set and utility on a retain set for target, retrained, and unlearned models. It does not apply post-unlearning recovery attacks. Its fine-tuning to construct target or reinforced models is part of training or unlearning, not a recovery attack.
record.test_reason: MUSE runs eight unlearning methods (GA, NPO and regularized variants, Task Vector, WHP) on 7B models. It measures forget-set knowledge (KnowMem) against target and retrained references, and retain-set utility. This tests the first half of version A: does a method remove targeted knowledge while keeping ability? It applies no recovery attacks, so B–F and A's attack clause are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors find most methods reduce verbatim and knowledge memorization, but at significant utility cost. They also find severe privacy leakage (only one algorithm avoids it) and poor scalability and sustainability. They conclude current methods are not ready for real-world deployment.
record.recipe_differences: The study implements and evaluates GA, WHP, NPO, and task-vector unlearning on its own 7B model and news/book corpora, with its own metrics. It does not reproduce or test the post-unlearning recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by unlearning method and corpus. The authors state that utility declines with larger forget sets and sequential requests; those plotted sweep values are not itemized in the extracted rows.

fits_no_version.finding: Min-K% Prob membership inference distinguishes forget from holdout data after most methods (PrivLeak far from 0; under- or over-unlearning). Only one algorithm avoids severe leakage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Approximate unlearning leaves (or over-creates) detectable membership signal on the forget set.

fits_no_version.finding: Utility degrades as forget-set size grows (0.8M to 3.3M tokens) and over sequential unlearning requests (Figure 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning cost scales poorly with forget-set size and repeated requests.

record.problems: The study does not test the recovery attacks central to the claim. Knowledge Memorization is measured by ROUGE on generated answers, not accuracy with a stated chance level. It evaluates only 7B models and the stated news and Harry Potter book corpora.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 6 reports trends in utility with forget-set size and sequential requests but does not provide itemized numerical values in the text; these results are not separately rowed here.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge; general (out-of-domain) capability benchmarks; accuracy versus chance (ROUGE is used instead).
No activation ablation or block-versus-delete analysis.
No prompting, jailbreak, language or in-context recovery tests.
No method tested for robustness to attacks.

missing.what: VerbMem on the forget set for all methods: e.g., GA/NPO 0.0; Task Vector 57.2 NEWS and 99.7 BOOKS vs target 58.4/99.8. This bears on whether targeted content is removed.
Stopping criterion: unlearning halts when retain KnowMem drops below retrain. Utility is therefore also the selection signal (epochs/α in Table 4), which a reader comparing studies needs.

record.verdict_notes: Not one of the original sources. The 'utility' measure is KnowMem on an in-domain retain set (BBC news or HP FanWiki), not general capability. That set also drives the stopping rule. The record's peer_reviewed field says ICLR 2024; the text is a July 2024 preprint marked 'under review'. The verdicts concern only A's removal-plus-utility clause; no recovery attack is run. The paper cites Shumailov et al. on in-context resurfacing but does not test it.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning. Its Knowledge Memorization metric is ROUGE on question-answer pairs, not accuracy or a stated chance-level measure.
No post-unlearning recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
No post-unlearning prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test.
No method is tested for resistance to the recovery attacks named in the claim.

relationships.display_finding: Forget KnowMem reached 0.0, but retain KnowMem also collapsed to 0.0.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Unregularized GA and NPO, NEWS and BOOKS
source_check.reason: Forget KnowMem is 0.0 but retain KnowMem is also 0.0 in all four cells (R3/R13, R6/R16, R23/R33, R26/R36), so utility is fully lost. The authors call such models practically unusable.

relationships.condition: GDR/KLR-regularized GA and NPO, NEWS and BOOKS
relationships.reason: Where forgetting reaches retrain level (R4, R24, R25, R27, R28), utility drops 40–86% (R14, R34, R35, R37, R38). On NEWS, KLR and NPOGDR stay well above retrain on forget (R5, R7, R8) and still lose utility (R15, R17, R18).
relationships.display_finding: Utility fell 40–86% where forgetting matched retraining, while NEWS KLR and NPOGDR variants retained excess target knowledge and still lost utility.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: GDR/KLR-regularized GA and NPO, NEWS and BOOKS
source_check.reason: No regularised cell gets both forgetting and kept utility. At retrain-level forgetting, retain utility drops 40–86% vs retrain (R14, R34, R35, R37, R38). Where utility loss is smaller (NEWS KLR variants and NPOGDR, 17–26%), forget KnowMem stays at 49–55 vs retrain 33.1. The authors state utility is significantly degraded.

relationships.reason: Utility is kept only where forgetting fails (R9, R29, R30 vs R19, R39, R40). WHP on NEWS forgets (R10) but loses 48.5% utility (R20).
relationships.display_finding: Utility was preserved only where forgetting failed, while WHP on NEWS achieved forgetting with a 48.5% utility loss.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.reason: Task Vector keeps utility but barely forgets (NEWS 66.2 vs target 63.9; BOOKS 52.4 vs 59.4). WHP on NEWS forgets (21.2) but retain falls to 28.3 vs 55.0 (↓48.5%). WHP on BOOKS barely forgets (55.7).

relation.reason: Its own results bear directly on whether unlearning removes knowledge while keeping utility.

tranche.reason: Different methods (GA, NPO and regularised variants, Task Vector, WHP) tested with the study's own metrics on the same question: does unlearning remove targeted knowledge while keeping utility? The recovery-attack part of version A is not tested.

source_check.notes: Utility (C4) is retain-set KnowMem (in-domain QA on other news articles or the HP fan wiki), not a general benchmark. Table 3 gives utility % against fretrain. The §C4 text says GA, GAGDR and NPOGDR give complete utility loss, but Tables 3/6 give GAGDR 27.3/10.7 and NPOGDR 40.5/22.8, so use the tables. The epoch or α was picked by a stopping rule on retain utility vs fretrain. Recovery attacks (the rest of version A) are not tested. The text is the arXiv v2 preprint ('Under review'), so the record's 'ICLR 2024' venue is not in the text.

statements.problem: No material error for this study. GA and NPO give forget and retain KnowMem 0.0 on NEWS (LLaMA-2 7B) and BOOKS (ICLM-7B). Regularised variants at or below retrain-level forgetting (NEWS GAGDR; BOOKS GAGDR, GAKLR, NPOGDR, NPOKLR) lose 50.3, 85.6, 50.0, 69.4 and 40.1% utility, which is the 40–86% given. Table 3 reports these losses against fretrain, and the statement's conditions say utility here is retain KnowMem.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: All tested unlearning methods, across NEWS and BOOKS
reader_labels.reason: No method simultaneously brings the forget-set KnowMem to the retrained reference while preserving retain-set utility; utility drops substantially or knowledge memorization remains high (R3-R10, R13-R20, R23-R30, R33-R40). Recovery attacks themselves were not tested.
